verses.1: Why are times not kept by the Almighty, and why do those who know Him not see His days?
verses.2: Boundaries are transgressed by the wicked; they seize flocks and drive them off.
verses.3: They lead away the donkey of orphans, they take the ox of widows as pledge.
verses.4: They push the poor from the road together; the poor of the land are hidden.
verses.5: Look, they are like wild donkeys in the desert, they rush out to find prey, they go forth to look for food in the waste.
verses.6: They cut down in the field at night, and the vineyard of the wicked they strip bare.
verses.7: They lie in the cold without a covering, and the sackcloth is their covering.
verses.8: Drenched from the snow of the mountains, and without shelter, they huddle beneath the rock.
verses.9: They seize the orphan's inheritance and oppress the poor.
verses.10: They lie about without clothing, and the hungry carry the sheaf.
verses.11: They dwell among the cliffs, they dig in the rocks and thirst.
verses.12: From the city of the dead they are snatched, and the soul of the slain cries out, yet God does not give His judgment.
verses.13: These are the ones who have rebelled against light, they do not know His ways, nor do they walk in His paths.
verses.14: The murderer rises at dawn, the poor and the needy are slain, and at night he is as a thief.
verses.15: And the eye of the adulterer watches, saying, "The eye will not see me," and he sets a veil over his face.
verses.16: He digs in darkness, they seal themselves in the day, they do not know light.
verses.17: For to them the morning is like the shadow of death, for they know not how to shun the shadow of death.
verses.18: He is lighter than the surface of the water; their portion is cursed on the earth, they do not turn from the ways of the vineyards.
verses.19: Their roots are scorched, their branches are dried— because they stole the cradle of orphans.
verses.20: Let his mother forget him, let his sweetness be taken away. Let them not remember him again, and let him be broken like a wicked tree.
verses.21: One who tends a barren woman will not bear fruit, and a widow will not be made to flourish.
verses.22: And he who strengthens the weak by his might will rise and not trust in the living.
verses.23: He gives him confidence and he leans— but his eyes are on his ways.
verses.24: They rise a little, and they are not there; they are brought low like all, they are scattered like the heads of ears.
verses.25: And if not so, who is there to disprove me, to set my words as nothing?

notes:
Notes
- v. 17: "the shadow of death" is a consistent rendering of the Hebrew "צלמות" in context.
- v. 18: "lighter than the surface of the water" reflects the Hebrew metaphor, not literal weight.
- v. 24: "the heads of ears" (heads of grain) is a poetic image, rendered clearly in English.

[1] Why are times not kept by the Almighty, and why do those who know Him not see His days?
[2] Boundaries are transgressed by the wicked; they seize flocks and drive them off.
[3] They lead away the donkey of orphans, they take the ox of widows as pledge.
[4] They push the poor from the road together; the poor of the land are hidden.
[5] Look, they are like wild donkeys in the desert, they rush out to find prey, they go forth to look for food in the waste.
[6] They cut down in the field at night, and the vineyard of the wicked they strip bare.
[7] They lie in the cold without a covering, and the sackcloth is their covering.
[8] Drenched from the snow of the mountains, and without shelter, they huddle beneath the rock.
[9] They seize the orphan's inheritance and oppress the poor.
[10] They lie about without clothing, and the hungry carry the sheaf.
[11] They dwell among the cliffs, they dig in the rocks and thirst.
[12] From the city of the dead they are snatched, and the soul of the slain cries out, yet God does not give His judgment.
[13] These are the ones who have rebelled against light, they do not know His ways, nor do they walk in His paths.
[14] The murderer rises at dawn, the poor and the needy are slain, and at night he is as a thief.
[15] And the eye of the adulterer watches, saying, "The eye will not see me," and he sets a veil over his face.
[16] He digs in darkness, they seal themselves in the day, they do not know light.
[17] For to them the morning is like the shadow of death, for they know not how to shun the shadow of death.
[18] He is lighter than the surface of the water; their portion is cursed on the earth, they do not turn from the ways of the vineyards.
[19] Their roots are scorched, their branches are dried— because they stole the cradle of orphans.
[20] Let his mother forget him, let his sweetness be taken away. Let them not remember him again, and let him be broken like a wicked tree.
[21] One who tends a barren woman will not bear fruit, and a widow will not be made to flourish.
[22] And he who strengthens the weak by his might will rise and not trust in the living.
[23] He gives him confidence and he leans— but his eyes are on his ways.
[24] They rise a little, and they are not there; they are brought low like all, they are scattered like the heads of ears.
[25] And if not so, who is there to disprove me, to set my words as nothing?

Notes
- v. 17: "the shadow of death" is a consistent rendering of the Hebrew "צלמות" in context.
- v. 18: "lighter than the surface of the water" reflects the Hebrew metaphor, not literal weight.
- v. 24: "the heads of ears" (heads of grain) is a poetic image, rendered clearly in English.
